summary.title: Web Browser Engineering
summary.one_liner: You learn how a web browser works by building a basic but complete one in a couple thousand lines of Python, from HTTP networking through HTML parsing, layout, CSS, JavaScript, and rendering.
takeaways: Browsers can be understood by building one: download pages over HTTP, draw to a window, and lay out text.
HTML is parsed into a tree, and CSS styles are parsed and applied to that tree before layout.
Interactive features come from DOM changes and event handling, with an event loop and rendering pipeline scheduling work.
Security topics such as cookies, logins, XSS, and CSRF are covered alongside form submission and servers.
Later chapters cover compositing, accessibility, embedded content, and reusing computation for efficiency.
summary.summary: This is the online book Web Browser Engineering, which builds a basic but complete web browser in a couple thousand lines of Python. The chapters move through downloading pages over URLs and HTTP, drawing to a window, text formatting, parsing HTML into a tree, inline and block layout, CSS, links and browser chrome, form submission, and running scripts that change the DOM. Later chapters cover cookies and security, visual effects, the event loop and threads, GPU-based animation, keyboard and accessibility support, images and iframes, and invalidation. The page itself lists the chapter topics and notes that the book is available in print and in Korean and Japanese translations.
